title: Jude and the Extraction
premise: Ulyana Zhou, a deniable asset for the Meridian Liaison Office—an embassy that exists on no map—receives a meeting request from his handler three days after the man's confirmed death. The invitation lures him into a rogue operation: extract Dr. Ilse Brandt, a bioweapons defector, from a hostile port city before a dawn flight. But Ulyana discovers the dead handler orchestrated the job as a posthumous test, and Ilse may be deliberate bait for the mole inside Meridian who killed him. To survive, Ulyana must decide whether loyalty to his found family at the office matters more than the truth they've been feeding him—and in the final hours, he burns his own cover to expose the mole, gets Ilse onto the plane, and walks away from the only home he's ever known.
about_author: Emrys Sandoval is the pen name of a former logistics contractor who spent a decade in cities that appear on no itineraries. He writes thrillers about people whose jobs depend on being forgettable, and he still keeps a go-bag packed.

chapters.title: The Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Ulyana Zhou, POV. Three days after burying his handler Marcus Vane, Ulyana receives a calendar invite in Vane's exact style, for a meeting tomorrow. He checks the morgue photos twice. The chapter establishes his polished lie of a life and ends with him deciding to go, because ignoring Vane was never an option. Beat: dread wrapped in routine.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Flashback-woven tour of the Meridian Liaison Office: the fixers, the analysts, the kitchen where someone always cooks at 2 a.m. We meet Deputy Director Okafor, who denies Vane sent anything, and young analyst Priya, who quietly flags the invite's metadata as authentic. Beat: warmth of found family shadowed by the first crack of doubt.

chapters.title: What Vane Knew
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Following the invite's dead-drop coordinates, Ulyana finds a burner phone preloaded with a single file: Vane's private dossier alleging a mole inside Meridian, and a name redacted. The file includes an extraction job—Dr. Ilse Brandt, port city of Varna, wheels up at dawn in four days. Beat: grief curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Offer You Can't Refuse Politely
chapters.summary: Okafor, POV. Okafor assigns Ulyana to the Brandt extraction officially, insisting Vane's invite is a hostile spoof. Privately, Okafor orders the operation's comms monitored. The reader sees Okafor's hands shake—ambiguity: fear of the mole, or fear of exposure? Beat: the family begins watching itself.

chapters.title: Packing the Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Priya, POV. Priya, who idolizes Ulyana, is ordered to be his comms support and hates that she must also report on him. She patches a backdoor into the monitoring feed—her own small betrayal of the office for loyalty to a person. Beat: loyalty splitting along personal fault lines.

chapters.title: Varna, Night One
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Ulyana lands in Varna under a shipping-clerk cover and makes contact with Ilse Brandt, a defector who is sharper and less frightened than any asset he's handled. She asks him directly: 'Who invited you—the living or the dead?' Beat: first meeting; two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Tail
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. A surveillance team that isn't Russian, isn't local, and isn't Meridian's picks up Ulyana within hours—impossible unless someone inside gave his itinerary away. He runs a counter-surveillance dance through the port district and barely cleans his trail. Beat: paranoia becomes arithmetic—the mole is real.

chapters.title: Ilse's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. Ilse reveals she requested extraction only after Vane contacted her—before he died. She carries proof of a bioweapons program and knows Meridian's mole by a codename: LANTERN. She'll only fly with someone Vane trusted, which is why she tested Ulyana. Beat: the bait realizes she is the bait and chooses to be anyway.

chapters.title: Static on the Line
chapters.summary: Priya, POV. Monitoring Ulyana's feed, Priya hears a second voice splice into the channel—someone feeding the surveillance team. She traces the splice to an office terminal logged to a senior officer, but the logs wipe themselves before she can screenshot. Beat: proof exists for exactly as long as it takes to vanish.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Problem
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Ulyana's fallback safehouse is already burned; he moves Ilse to a fisherman's attic, off every grid. Cut off from Meridian, the two build an uneasy partnership over canned peaches and traded lies. Beat: found family in miniature, two people with no one else.

chapters.title: Okafor's Version
chapters.summary: Okafor, POV. Okafor recalls Ulyana, declaring the extraction compromised and Ilse a likely double agent. Ulyana refuses, going dark—formal treason. Okafor's chapter reveals she has known about LANTERN for months and has been feeding candidates into the fire to flush it out. Beat: the mentor's terrible arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Mole's Face
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Using Vane's dossier and Priya's partial trace, Ulyana narrows LANTERN to two men: operations chief Daniel Reyes, Vane's best friend, and Ulyana's own former partner, Tomas Hale. A staged leak to each produces only one reaction. Beat: the answer is the person who taught him the trade.

chapters.title: What Tomas Taught Me
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Flashback chapter: how Hale recruited, trained, and sheltered a directionless Ulyana—every kindness now re-readable as cultivation. Present-day Hale contacts Ulyana openly, offering to extract him both, claiming Vane was LANTERN's true target. Beat: the most dangerous lie is the one you want to believe.

chapters.title: The Peaches Test
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. Ilse, a psychologist of manipulation, dissects Hale's approach and shows Ulyana the tells: Hale's offer contains information only LANTERN could have. Ulyana grieves in advance and agrees to feed Hale a false extraction route. Beat: loyalty to truth wins a round, at personal cost.

chapters.title: Feeding LANTERN
chapters.summary: Priya, POV. Priya risks everything, slipping Ulyana the real airfield data through the backdoor she built, while Meridian's official channel broadcasts the false route Hale will swallow. Okafor, watching Priya's anomaly, chooses not to report it. Beat: three quiet mutinies converging.

chapters.title: Hale's Move
chapters.summary: Hale, POV. Hale takes the bait—but not passively: he orders the surveillance team to hit the false route hard and personally heads to the real airfield, intending to put Ilse on a plane to his buyers instead, with Ulyana dead as a loose end. Beat: the antagonist's competence makes the trap symmetrical—now both sides know the airfield.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes to Dawn
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. The clock chapter: Ulyana and Ilse move through the port's pre-dawn fog toward the airfield, surveillance team tearing apart the false route behind them. Vane's file reveals its last layer—a dead-man's switch that emails everything to every intelligence service in twelve hours unless Ulyana stops it. Beat: acceleration; every choice now costs something irreversible.

chapters.title: The Hangar
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. At the hangar, Hale is waiting, and the confrontation is less a gunfight than an argument with weapons: Hale offers Ulyana his old life back one final time. Ulyana refuses, they fight, and Ulyana wins ugly, wounding rather than killing him. Beat: the climax of loyalty vs. truth—choosing truth means losing the man who made him.

chapters.title: Wheels Up
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Ulyana gets Ilse aboard the dawn flight as the surveillance team's survivors close in. Okafor, having quietly burned Meridian's own protocols to cover his exit, gives him ninety seconds of air cover by phone. Ilse makes him promise to stop being invisible. Beat: triumph with a door closing behind it.

chapters.title: The Dead-Man's Hand
chapters.summary: Priya, POV. Back at Meridian, Vane's dead-man's switch fires anyway—Hale's people tripped it during the hangar fight—and the office's secrets begin landing in inboxes worldwide. Priya must decide in minutes whether to warn Okafor or let the institution that lied to them all burn. Beat: truth arrives whether or not anyone is ready.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Meridian
chapters.summary: Okafor, POV. Hale is arrested at the airfield; Meridian survives, gutted and renamed, with Okafor resigning to testify. Priya declines promotion, keeping her backdoor. Okafor's last act is deleting Ulyana from every file—making him truly invisible, as a gift. Beat: the found family endures, transformed by what it now knows.

chapters.title: A Man Who Can Be Found
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Epilogue. Months later, Ulyana lives openly under his real name in a coastal town where Ilse, relocated and safe, sends him postcards he answers. He unpacks the go-bag at last. A new invitation arrives—unsigned this time—and he smiles, because now he chooses. Beat: belonging, finally, on his own terms.
